record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Determine which Bergman zero sequences A have the property that every z-invariant subspace M of L^2_a(D) containing I(A), the functions that vanish on A, has index 1.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 14 Determine the zero sequences A

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the Bergman space, the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2 \, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A closed subspace $M\subset L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called $z$-invariant if $zM\subset M$. The index of a nonzero $z$-invariant subspace $M$ is defined by
$$\mathrm{ind}(M) = \dim(M\ominus zM).$$
A sequence $A=\{a_n\}\subset \mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities) is called a Bergman zero sequence if there exists a nonzero $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ vanishing on $A$ (counting multiplicities). For such a sequence $A$, let
$$I(A) = \{f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D}) : f \text{ vanishes on } A \text{ counting multiplicities}\}.$$

Characterize the Bergman zero sequences $A\subset\mathbb{D}$ with the following property: every $z$-invariant subspace $M$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ with $I(A)\subset M$ satisfies $\mathrm{ind}(M)=1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Bergman zero sequences whose associated vanishing-ideal subspace forces all containing z-invariant subspaces to have index one appears to remain open. Related literature on the index of invariant subspaces in the Bergman space (including constructions of subspaces of arbitrary and infinite index) discusses this circle of questions but does not provide a known characterization.
